questions.q: Which three things must come together to turn a passion into income?
a: Passion, skills and customers
Passion, savings and luck
Skills, marketing and investors
Customers, advertising and scale
questions.why: Lesson 1 says passion is only one third, alongside the skills you have and the people who pay.

questions.q: What does the pizza example show about turning a passion into a business?
a: Making pizza for paying guests turns a taste into a service
Food businesses are the cheapest and easiest to launch
Friends will always support a new venture generously
Enthusiasm alone is enough if you charge a low price
questions.why: Lesson 1 contrasts enjoying pizza with making it for others who cannot do it themselves.

questions.q: How does the summary suggest you treat costs in a microbusiness?
a: As a way to prioritize what actually drives sales
As a problem best solved with outside funding
As the main measure of how well you are doing
As something to cut by hiring cheaper freelancers
questions.why: Lesson 2 says limited money forces you to invest only where it directly drives revenue.

questions.q: Which questions should a one-page business plan answer?
a: What you sell, to whom, why they buy and how you are paid
Who your rivals are, your budget, your staff and your logo
Your mission, vision, values and long-term goals
How much you will earn, save, invest and donate
questions.why: Lesson 3 reduces planning to those four practical questions and leaves the rest for later.

questions.q: What does the author say to do with unsolicited business advice?
a: Ignore it and trust your own judgment
Weigh it carefully with your family
Test it before deciding anything
Ask a mentor to evaluate it
questions.why: Lesson 3 warns that everyone becomes an expert once you start, and tells you to do you.
